title: Pinnacle scale: figures, definitions and evidence

metrics.label: Structured developmental records
metrics.meaning: A large record system can preserve observations across a child’s developmental journey, supporting continuity and review.
metrics.basis: Reported in the 7 September 2026 handout. Database row/event counts at 17 July 2026.
metrics.boundary: Session entries, assessment observations, technique ratings and other structured events. The evidence does not identify every record as an AI-training example or establish clinical effectiveness.

metrics.label: Cumulative therapy services reported
metrics.meaning: The useful family question is how the experience recorded across services informs a clear plan and review for your child.
metrics.basis: 31,052,382 under the practitioner reports’ service-counting criteria, at 17 July 2026.
metrics.boundary: The defined total includes assessments, screenings and parent training. It is not established as 31 million successful one-to-one therapy sessions; service volume and clinical success are separate measures.

metrics.label: Early-intervention technique repository
metrics.meaning: A technique library is useful when a practitioner selects and adapts activities to a child’s goals, interests and everyday routines.
metrics.basis: 130,000 techniques: management-supplied update received 18 September 2026. The 7 September handout reports an earlier 90,000+ library.
metrics.boundary: The updated repository count has not been reconciled to a dated inventory extract. The reviewed UDIN reports do not establish this figure, and technique count does not mean 130,000 separately validated interventions.

metrics.label: Beneficiary / family registrations reported
metrics.meaning: Behind each registration is a family seeking support. A family’s own goals and progress reviews remain the measure that matters to them.
metrics.basis: 792,614 unique beneficiary/family registrations under the stated criteria, at 17 July 2026.
metrics.boundary: This is the defined registration measure. It is not a count of unique children with independently verified outcomes, and it does not itself measure family empowerment.

metrics.label: Countries of family origin reported
metrics.meaning: Families may connect with developmental support across borders, including through remote delivery where available.
metrics.basis: Company-reported international reach in the July 2026 dossier, including remote delivery.
metrics.boundary: Countries of family origin are different from countries with a physical Pinnacle centre. The reviewed practitioner reports do not establish this country count.

metrics.label: Centres in the reported network
metrics.meaning: A network becomes relevant locally. Find your centre, its facility identifier and the source behind each listed document.
metrics.basis: Network figure reported in the September handout. The practitioner-report criteria separately identify 49 operational centres at 17 July 2026.
metrics.boundary: Network size, operational status and HFR identifiers are different measures. The full supplied HFR workbook is reconciled with certificate copies below; an HFR entry does not establish clinical outcomes or replace location-specific licensing.
